why: Personal, story-led posts do well on r/sleep and position the founder as someone who gets the problem.
rules: Self-promotion is not allowed. Personal account, no product, no links. Post after the introductions, one per day through the week. A brand-new account with little karma gets auto-removed in most subs, so comment helpfully in the sub for a few days first.
title: Scuba diving taught me more about falling asleep than any sleep hack did
text:
I've done 70-odd dives. The thing nobody tells you about diving is how slow your mind gets underwater. You breathe slowly because you have to, and after a dive I'd sleep better than any night in the city.

Back on land with a desk job, my problem was never being tired. My mind just wouldn't switch off at 11 PM. What helped me copy that underwater feeling was slow breathing for five minutes in bed (long exhale, roughly 4 in and 6 out), the phone in another room, and the same wake time every day, even on Sundays.

I'm curious what your version of this is. Is there an activity that reliably gives you a great night's sleep afterwards, and have you found a way to get that at home?
